draft.title: Establishment and growth
card: The business life cycle describes the stages a business can pass through over time. Establishment and growth are the first two stages.
the start-up stage. Few customers know the business, so sales are low while start-up costs are high. Cash flow problems are common, which makes this the riskiest stage.
sales and profits rise as more customers buy. The business often hires more staff, moves to bigger premises or opens new locations.
Growth brings new challenges. The owner can no longer do everything, so tasks must be handed to managers. Expansion also needs more finance, such as loans or new owners.
draft.remember: Establishment is a fight to survive. Growth is a fight to manage and fund getting bigger.

a.q: Which sign best shows that a business is in the establishment stage?
opts: Low sales and trouble paying bills on time
Rising profits and plans to hire more staff
Owner hands daily tasks to new managers
Taking out loans to open new branches
a.why: Low sales and cash flow problems mark the risky start of a business. Hiring staff, handing tasks to managers and borrowing to open branches all come with growth, when sales are already rising.
a.clue: Think about a business that few customers know yet.

b.q: Priya opened a bakery in Ballarat two years ago. Sales have doubled, she has hired four staff and plans a second shop. What challenge is she most likely to face now?
opts: Finding finance and managing a bigger team
Attracting customers who do not know her
Covering start-up costs from very low sales
Rising profits mean she needs no new finance
b.why: Rising sales, new staff and a second shop show the growth stage, where managing more people and funding expansion are the main challenges. Unknown customers and low sales belong to establishment, which Priya has moved past. Rising profits rarely pay for a whole new shop, so growth usually needs extra finance.
b.clue: Which stage do doubling sales and new staff point to?

a.best: Low sales and trouble paying bills on time

b.best: Finding finance and managing a bigger team
